hypothesis: Asking the model to draft a concrete plan first will force it to commit to task-specific assumptions (budget, dates, scale), and those assumptions will be more grounded decision-critical unknowns than abstract brainstorming — yielding better coverage than prior RAG variants.
technique: A two-stage FM pipeline: stage 1 uses the stock 3B to draft a concrete execution plan and explicitly surface the assumptions it was forced to make; stage 2 feeds those surfaced assumptions into the exp003 RAG few-shot scaffold to phrase and atomise them into 7 final questions.
result: Scored 0.245 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), the worst of any RAG-derived variant and −0.075 below the exp003 best (0.320). Coverage collapsed to 2 (down from 3), because planning-first causes the 3B to surface minor logistical specifics (seating, transport, paperwork) rather than high-level decision-critical unknowns, and the extra FM stage reintroduced naturalness and sanity failures; hypothesis firmly falsified — discarded.

stages.text: Draft concrete plan, surface forced assumptions
